card.intuition: An inverted index (word → list of documents) stored across shards, queried in parallel and merged. Documents are ingested by a pipeline that tokenizes, normalizes, and ranks content; queries hit the index shards, which return top results scored by relevance.
card.analogy: A library's back-of-book concordance: instead of reading every book to find a word, you look up the word in an alphabetized index that tells you which page of which book mentions it. The index is split across many tiny libraries, and a central librarian merges the pages each returns.
card.time_complexity: Query is O(t · shards) where t is terms matched and shards are searched in parallel; each shard returns its top-k in O(k log k).
card.space_complexity: The inverted index and the original documents both scale with corpus size; index size is typically 10–20% of raw text.
when_to_use: Full-text search over a very large, changing document corpus
Relevance-ranked retrieval over keyword or phrase queries
Near-real-time ingestion (web search, product search, log search)
gotchas: Indexing and querying must be decoupled: documents are searchable only after the async pipeline finishes
Ranking quality depends on the scorer — naive term frequency punishes common words and favors huge documents unless normalized

steps.annotation: Documents are harvested and pushed into the ingestion pipeline.
The pipeline tokenizes text and builds an inverted index mapping words to documents.
The index is distributed across shards so each holds a slice of the vocabulary.
A query fans out to every shard in parallel; each returns its top-ranked hits.
Results from all shards are merged and re-ranked before being returned to the user.

exercise.prompt: A search cluster indexes 40 million documents across 8 shards. If each shard can return its top 10 results for a query in 20 ms, what is the approximate end-to-end query latency if shards run in parallel and merge takes 5 ms?
exercise.starter_code:
shard_query_ms = 20
merge_ms = 5

end_to_end_ms = shard_query_ms + merge_ms
# Result is ___ ms
hints: Shards run in parallel, so we take the max shard time, not the sum
